tools.name: find_programs
tools.description: Finds online telehealth programs in one U.S. specialty and sorts them by lowest advertised monthly price. Use it when the user asks which online program is cheapest, which programs offer a treatment (e.g. compounded tirzepatide, TRT, sermorelin), which are LegitScript-certified, or which fit a budge

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_categories" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Lists the U.S. telehealth specialties this server covers, with each specialty’s slug, the treatment keys it accepts (for example semaglutide, tirzepatide, trt, …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_programs" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
